item.title: ManningCast slumps to 517,000 viewers, while the Next Gen Stats version surges
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The bloom is off the ManningCast rose.
item.content:encoded:
The bloom is off the ManningCast rose.

The critically-acclaimed alt cast continues to lose viewership. Via Andrew Marchand of The Athletic, the latest edition from the Week 7 game between the Cowboys and Eagles attracted only 517,000 viewers.

At one point, the Peyton & Eli show routinely racked up more than a million viewers per episode. Once ESPN beefed up its primary broadcast with Joe Buck and Troy Aikman, however, the tide began to slowly turn.

Now, it's unclear where the bottom will be.

Complicating the situation is the new Next Gen Stats broadcast that Disney has added to NFL Network. For Week 7, 499,000 tuned in. That's more than the NFLN version attracted a week earlier, when the 469,000-viewer audience for Commanders-49ers significantly outpaced the ESPN2 McAfee alt cast, at 351,000. (The next McAfee alt cast will likely see a viewership decline in Utah.)

It's ultimately no surprise. The ESPN alt casts do not bring in viewers who would otherwise not watch the game. It simply pulls viewers away from the primary broadcast.

Most people want to just watch the game. Once the guests arrive for the ManningCast, it becomes a podcast with a football game playing in the background.

Given the ongoing trend, the ESPN2 alt casts don't feel sustainable. Whatever they cost, it's an expense without any real added revenue.

The best result could be to move the Next Gen Stats version to the bigger platform of ESPN2 — and then to lure Peyton (and possibly Eli) into the primary booth with Buck.

Surely, ESPN already has a post-Aikman plan in its back pocket. While some think it will result in the hiring of Greg Olsen, a merger of the ManningCast with the main broadcast could be the best way forward, for everyone.

item.title: Raiders OT DJ Glaze: Bills S Sam Franklin did spit at me, but it is what it is
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Bills safety Sam Franklin will be available for this Sunday's game against the Ravens after making a successful appeal of a one-game suspension.
item.content:encoded:
Bills safety Sam Franklin will be available for this Sunday's game against the Ravens after making a successful appeal of a one-game suspension.

Franklin was suspended for spitting at Raiders right tackle DJ Glaze late in a Week 6 win, but the penalty was reduced to a $14,926 fine after an appeal last week. That change has not changed Glaze's account of what happened.

Glaze said on Wednesday that Franklin "was, like, face to face, and he just let it rip," but believes the suspension was overturned because there was not the same kind of clear evidence that led to Franklin's teammate C.J. Gardner-Johnson's ejection and suspension for spitting at Glaze's teammate Brock Bowers.

“That’s why I feel like it kind of got taken away. . . . He did,” Glaze said, via TheAthletic.com. “He said he didn’t. You know, he did. But it is what it is at this point. It happened. And the NFL did what they did about it.”

Franklin has denied the allegation, which was lodged by the Raiders and which Bills head coach Joe Brady dismissed as "hearsay" during his own press conference on Wednesday.

item.title: Titans agree to trade Jeffery Simmons to Bears
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Chicago will send Tennessee two first-round picks and a fourth-round pick to complete the deal.
item.content:encoded:
All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons told reporters on Wednesday that as far as he knew, he wasn’t going to be traded before the deadline.

But maybe he packed a go bag anyway, just in case — because now he needs it.

According to multiple reports, the Titans have agreed to trade Simmons to the Bears.

To complete the deal, Chicago receives Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Tennessee will receive 2027 and 2028 first-round picks along with a fourth-round pick in 2027.

Simmons, 29, is a four-time Pro Bowler and was an AP first-team All-Pro for the first time last season. He registered a career-high 11.0 sacks with 17 tackles for loss and 21 quarterback hits in 2025.

The No. 19 overall pick of the 2019 draft, Simmons has tallied 46.5 sacks, 72 tackles for loss, and 96 QB hits in his career.

In seven games this season, Simmons has registered 4.0 sacks, six TFLs, and nine QB hits.

The Titans and Simmons had agreed to a three-year $105.8 million contract extension before the season. Now, Simmons will head to Chicago to help a defense that currently ranks No. 8 in yards allowed and No. 9 in points allowed.

item.title: Jon Gruden's case against the NFL isn't going well — and it's his own fault
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Said the presiding judge in a recent hearing: “We have no reason to trust representations by Mr. Gruden."
item.content:encoded:
Jon Gruden asked for it, and Jon Gruden definitely is getting it.

After a legal odyssey that somehow staved off the NFL's obsession to force his five-year-old lawsuit into arbitration controlled by the league, Gruden won the ability to have his claims litigated in open court. Now that the litigation is moving forward, Gruden is drowning in the obligations of the discovery process.

In August, the presiding judge publicly criticized Gruden and his lawyers for "lack of compliance with the rules." More recently, it got worse for Gruden.

A lot worse.

Michael McCann of Sportico has obtained a transcript of a recent hearing regarding the ongoing efforts of the NFL to secure information to which the league is entitled, under the so-called rules of civil procedure. And the transcript sends an unmistakable message: Judge Joe Hardy seems to suspect that Gruden could be actively hiding evidence that could harm his case.

The current focal point is a phantom BlackBerry device. It existed, and now it doesn't.

"So did your client lie to you about a BlackBerry?" Judge Hardy said at one point during the hearing.

"It’s not a lie, Your Honor, it’s a mistake," attorney Adam Hosmer-Henner responded. "And what [Gruden] told me is that he had an old BlackBerry that he couldn’t turn on."

The judge apparently senses that Gruden's side is playing a shell game with the BlackBerry device in question.

"Did anybody from your office ever check to see if there was an actual BlackBerry?" Judge Hardy asked Hosmer-Henner.

"Mr. Gruden resides in Florida," Hosmer-Henner said. "We did not send an individual to rummage around his house to look for a BlackBerry. And what we did do is promptly respond to interrogatory responses providing all this information. With regard to the forensic collection, Mr. Gruden was at an event at the White House last week. He flew back that night in order to allow the forensic examiners selected by the NFL to go through his electronic devices and —"

"So let me interject there, too, because if you can’t tell, this process is frustrating," Judge Hardy said. "And you, on behalf of your client, keep saying things that seem to indicate, well, Mr. Gruden is super important and super special. And, you know, we should accommodate his schedule. For example, you just mentioned, well, he was at an event at the White House."

At one point during the hearing, Judge Hardy said this: “We have no reason to trust representations by Mr. Gruden."

Judge Hardy, per McCann, ordered Gruden to compensate the league for a portion of the attorneys' fees incurred in connection with the ongoing effort to force him to comply with the rules. That's an unusual development in any civil case, and it underscores Judge Hardy's growing frustration with Gruden and his lawyers.

Here's why it's a major problem for Gruden. The same judge who has come to the conclusion that the "representations by Mr. Gruden" should not be trusted will be making many key decisions about the merits of Gruden's case. If it proceeds to trial, Gruden will testify under the supervision of Judge Hardy.

And Gruden, who has a strong will, a quick temper, and a profane vocabulary, will be scrutinized very carefully by a judge who has already decided that he has "no reason to trust representations by Mr. Gruden."

So, no, it's not going well for Gruden. And it's his own fault. At best, he has failed to honor the duty to comply with the rules of the legal process he initiated. At worst — and as the judge undoubtedly suspects — Gruden possibly is trying to hide a device that may contain communications that could hurt, if not kill, his entire case.

On the surface, the idea that someone connected to the NFL weaponized supposedly confidential emails from an unrelated investigation to force Gruden out of his head-coaching job with the Raiders during the 2021 season is troubling. It becomes impossible for Gruden (who is already operating at a disadvantage due to the objectively problematic contents of the emails that were leaked) to prove a violation of applicable legal principles if he creates the impression that he's not cooperating with the process.

Or, even worse, if he is deliberately and actively trying to conceal other emails and/or text messages.

At this point, it becomes critical for Gruden to do anything and everything he can to regain the trust of the judge. Without that, it's just a matter of time before Gruden loses his case — and possibly ends up being required to reimburse the NFL for millions of dollars in fees and expenses incurred in defending itself against a case that Gruden seems to not be taking as seriously as he should.

item.title: Jeffery Simmons: As far as I know, I'll be here after trade deadline
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons signed a three-year contract extension with the Titans this offseason, but that hasn't stopped his name from popping up on lists of candidates to be traded ahead of the November 10 trade deadline.
item.content:encoded:
Defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons signed a three-year contract extension with the Titans this offseason, but that hasn't stopped his name from popping up on lists of candidates to be traded ahead of the November 10 trade deadline.

With the Titans off to a 1-6 start and all signs pointing to another dismal finish in the standings, some have wondered if they will deal Simmons in an effort to stock up on assets that could start pushing things in a better direction. That topic was brought up to Simmons on Wednesday and he said he has not heard anything at this point that leads him to believe he will be on the move.

"Each and every day I wake up, my goal is to be where my feet are at," Simmons said, via the team's website. "I'm never looking ahead, just being in the moment each and every day. I don't worry about the things that I can't control. Those types of things are also a distraction — that's a lot of fans and outside media. I haven't heard anything from my agent, I haven't heard anything from this organization. As far as I know, I am going to be here."

It only takes a couple of phone calls for that to change and the prospect of adding a player like Simmons to the defensive front could lead a contender to make the Titans an offer they won't refuse before the curtain drops on this year's trade window.

item.title: Zay Flowers: You know Lamar Jackson, he wants to play
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson was officially a full participant in Wednesday's practice, which ostensibly puts him on course to start Sunday's game against the Bills.
item.content:encoded:
Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson was officially a full participant in Wednesday's practice, which ostensibly puts him on course to start Sunday's game against the Bills.

But with the way this injury situation has gone, it's probably unwise to make any predictions about Jackson's status.

Still, receiver Zay Flowers noted while speaking to reporters on Wednesday how much of a lift it is to have Jackson on the practice field, noting Jackson's desire to be effective on Sundays.

“Oh, man, you know Lamar, Lamar wants to play. He wants to play when he is fully healthy,” Flowers said, via transcript from the team. “And seeing him out there today, obviously it gave everybody a smile on their face.

“He is the same player. He is the same person. He wasn't trying to force anything. He wasn't trying to make everybody overexcited. He just came out and did what he normally does.”

While the Ravens won their first game without Jackson in the lineup, they’ve dropped the last two to division rivals Cleveland and Cincinnati. Flowers says that’s not on backup QB Tyler Huntley.

“I felt like we could have gotten the win without Lamar last week,” Flowers said. “I don't think it was anything that had to do with 'Snoop' [Huntley]. I don't think Snoop played badly. I don't think Snoop played bad at all. I just think we weren't on the field long enough to help the defense out and keep the ball out of the Bengals' hands.

“So, having Lamar back definitely gives us a jumpstart and just seeing him back on the field running around [with] the plays he can create.”

The Ravens have scored just 23 points over the last two games — 10 against the Browns and 13 against the Bengals. They’ll likely need a lot more to keep up with the Bills on Sunday, and Jackson’s return would help in that endeavor.

item.title: Lamar Jackson a full participant in Wednesday's practice
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Ravens quarterback last had a full practice on Oct. 2.
item.content:encoded:
Ravens coach Jesse Minter would not reveal Lamar Jackson's participation level at Wednesday's practice. The injury report, though, shows the quarterback was a full participant.

It is Jackson's first full practice since Oct. 2, when he was a full participant with a back injury.

He has not played since Oct. 4, missing the past three games with a high ankle sprain.

Jackson was trending toward playing last week, with limited practices in all three on-field days. The Ravens initially listed him as questionable to play, but he was inactive for Sunday’s 35-13 loss to the Bengals.

The Ravens went 1-2 without Jackson, who is 3-1 with six passing touchdowns, one interception and one rushing touchdown.

Defensive lineman Calais Campbell (rest), safety Kyle Hamilton (knee), safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee), offensive guard Vega Ioane (knee), and linebacker Roquan Smith (knee) did not practice Wednesday.

Nose takcle John Jenkins (knee), offensive guard John Simpson (groin), offensive tackle Ronnie Stanley (rest/toe/ankle), cornerbcak T.J. Tampa Jr. (knee) and defensive tackle Broderick Washington (ankle) were limited.

item.title: Justin Jefferson: You want high production, but what we're doing is working
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Justin Jefferson is catching fewer passes and picking up fewer yards on a per-game basis than at any other point in his career, but he's not complaining about how the 2026 season has played out thus far.
item.content:encoded:
Justin Jefferson is catching fewer passes and picking up fewer yards on a per-game basis than at any other point in his career, but he's not complaining about how the 2026 season has played out thus far.

The reason why Jefferson is taking his relatively limited production in stride can be explained by a glance at the standings. The Vikings are the NFL's only undefeated team and Jefferson said on Wednesday that he's had years with big numbers and few wins in the past, so he's comfortable saying that he "definitely would love winning games over having that production."

Ideally, though, there'd be a balance that allows him a taste of both.

“That’s something you kinda have to be in the middle," Jefferson said. "Obviously you want to have high production. Obviously you want to be in the top category in all categories, but you have to look at the bigger picture and understand that we’re 6-0 and winning games. What we're doing right now is working. Obviously there's things to do better and things to fix on the offensive side of things, but all in all, it's coming together and we're doing things to win games."

The Vikings' defense-first approach has served them well to this point, but the schedule will be thorny in the coming weeks with the Lions, Bills, Packers, 49ers and Falcons on tap in November. They're likely going to need the offense to pull a little more weight at some point in that run and finding the right way to spring Jefferson loose would be a strong step in that direction.

item.title: Expect plenty of flags to fly on Thursday night between Panthers and Packers
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: On Thursday night, the planets will align in a very specific way.
item.content:encoded:
On Thursday night, the planets will align in a very specific way. And that could lead to more than a few penalties being called.

When the Panthers and Packers open Week 8, the game will pit the most-penalized team (the Packers, 9.3 per game) against the fourth most-penalized team (the Panthers, 8.7 per game). The Panthers also lead the league in penalty yards per game (79.2), while the Packers are second at 78.0 yards per game.

On top of that, referee Scott Novak's crew leads the league in penalties called per game (22.7) and penalties accepted per game (20.1).

Throw the ingredients together, and there could be a stew of stoppages on Thursday night.

Either way, it's something to monitor. Will the Packers and Panthers continue to draw an excess of penalty flags? Will Novak and crew continue to be flag-happy?

It could be a good idea to take a nap tomorrow afternoon. Thursday night's game could last a little longer than usual.

item.title: Mike McDaniel will remain the Chargers' offensive playcaller
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said that the team would spend their bye week "looking into everything" when it came to improving their offense and did not rule out a change involving offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel.
item.content:encoded:
Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said that the team would spend their bye week "looking into everything" when it came to improving their offense and did not rule out a change involving offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel.

McDaniel was not dismissed and he hasn't lost one of his primary job responsibilities either. Harbaugh confirmed at a press conference on Wednesday that McDaniel will continue to call the team's offensive plays when they return to action against the Rams on Sunday.

McDaniel's future was in doubt because the offense was a disaster over the course of the team's 0-6 start. They are averaging a league-worst 15 points per game while turning the ball over more frequently than any of the other 31 teams, so there's a lot of room for improvement once the team is back on the field.

The Rams aren't the easiest defense to face when you're trying to get an offense on track, but that's the challenge McDaniel will have to meet for the Chargers to find their first win of the season.

item.title: Garrett Wilson: I want to win, hopeful I can do it with Jets
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson's frustrations boiled over on the sideline during last Sunday's loss to the Dolphins, but he said on Wednesday that he's not looking for a move to another team ahead of the November 10 trade deadline.
item.content:encoded:
Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson's frustrations boiled over on the sideline during last Sunday's loss to the Dolphins, but he said on Wednesday that he's not looking for a move to another team ahead of the November 10 trade deadline.

Wilson told reporters he hasn't asked to be traded and said he understands that his "name flying around" as a possible trade candidate is just part of business in the NFL. Wilson was one of three 2022 first-round picks for the Jets and the other two — Sauce Gardner and Jermaine Johnson — have been traded away in the last year, which helps illustrate his point.

While Wilson was expressing his desire to stay put, he also made it clear that he puts a high priority on being part of a winning team. The Jets are 24-51 since Wilson joined the team.

"Yeah, I want to be here. I want to win games," Wilson said, via SNY. "That's the one thing we've been missing on here. I love it here. Do I love it more than I love winning? Nah, to be completely honest. But I'm hopeful. I’ve never been the best, most optimistic guy. But I done found a way and dug deep and I’ve been optimistic for three, four five years now. That’s why these ones each weekend hurt a little more."

The Jets have three first-round picks in 2027 already and Wilson's presence would make it likelier that the players added with those selections and over the rest of the offseason can propel them into playoff contention in the near future. It sounds like Wilson's patience for that to happen hasn't run out, but it does seem to be running thin in the wake of the franchise's latest deflating loss.

item.title: Packers LB Zaire Franklin won't play Thursday night
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin will miss another game.
item.content:encoded:
Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin will miss another game. It's not a surprise given the Packers play on Thursday night.

Coach Matt LaFleur announced Tuesday that Franklin will not play against the Panthers.

Franklin missed last week's game after getting accidentally kicked in Thursday's practice. He was diagnosed with a hairline fracture in his leg.

The Packers did not place him on injured reserve, believing he can return after missing fewer than four games.

Franklin ranks third on the team in tackles (41) and has two quarterback hits, a forced fumble and a pass breakup.

Ty’Ron Hopper took Franklin's spot in the lineup on Sunday, and Isaiah McDuffie wore the green dot in Franklin's stead.

item.title: Brian Thomas on rough stretch: Just want to flush it
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas is coming off two straight games without a catch and he didn't play at all in the second half of the team's Week 6 loss to the Texans.
item.content:encoded:
Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas is coming off two straight games without a catch and he didn't play at all in the second half of the team's Week 6 loss to the Texans.

Thomas had a drop in the first half of that game and his ongoing role on a team with several other receiving options has been the subject of conversation with the trade deadline less than two weeks away. Head coach Liam Coen said this week that he expects Thomas to make plays for the team in this week's game against the Colts and Thomas said on Wednesday that his approach coming out of the bye week has been to let go of what happened in the past.

"I really just wanted to flush it, come back ready with a different mindset and come back ready to go," Thomas said, via the team's website. "That was the biggest thing for me. . . . I feel I still know what I can do. I just have to go out and do it and go out there and show everybody what I can do."

Thomas had 87 catches for 1,282 yards as a rookie, but had 57 catches for 812 yards since Coen became the coach ahead of the 2025 season. That hasn't stopped the Jags from winning games — the Jags are 17-5 in the regular season with Coen — and those differing fortunes are a big reason why Thomas's name frequently comes up in trade rumors. Such talk has been rebuffed thus far, but Thomas will likely have to show more in the next couple of weeks to put them to bed for good.

item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: While players have been on the way out for the Colts this week, one key defender was back on the field on Wednesday.
item.content:encoded:
While players have been on the way out for the Colts this week, one key defender was back on the field on Wednesday.

Cornerback Sauce Gardner was officially limited in the day's session, according to Indianapolis' injury report.

The Colts held a walk-through instead of a full practice to start the week.

Gardner has been sidelined since the Oct. 18 loss to the Titans.

Gardner has recorded four passes defensed with 17 total tackles so far in 2026.

Cornerback Justin Walley (knee) and linebacker Bryce Boettcher (groin) did not participate on Wednesday.

Guard Matt Goncalves (ankle), receiver Anthony Gould (concussion), tight end Drew Ogletree (knee), defensive tackle Tim Smith (ankle), and tight end Tyler Warren (groin) were also listed as limited.

Warren has missed the last two games.

Linebacker CJ Allen (ankle) and linebacker Akeem Davis-Gaither (hand) were both full.

item.title: A.J. Brown: Sometimes I'm pushing through ankle injury, but no excuses
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Patriots wide receiver A.J.
item.content:encoded:
Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown remained limited in practice on Wednesday with the ankle injury that had him on injured reserve for four games and has contributed to his underwhelming production since returning to the lineup.

Brown has six catches on 16 targets in those two games and admitted in a Wednesday media session that he's still not feeling as explosive as he'd like when he's on the field. Brown said "sometimes I see it and sometimes I’m pushing through" before adding that nothing he's dealing with is an explanation for falling short of his desired level of play.

“I’m trying to put my best foot forward," Brown said. "I know obviously I’m working through something, but it’s no excuses. I made none in the first week I was out there. The things I can control, I try to control. That’s the only thing. Again, I don’t look at anything as positive or negative, if that’s what you’re looking for. It’s information.”

Brown got some extra time off with the Patriots playing last Thursday and we'll see if that makes a difference in his production when the Patriots visit the Dolphins this weekend.

item.title: Josh Downs on trade request: "I'm open to whatever"
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Downs did not explicitly confirm he'd requested a trade, but he didn't reject the notion of playing elsewhere when asked on Wednesday.
item.content:encoded:
Colts receiver Josh Downs did not directly confirm that he would like to be traded, but he effectively said he's open to a change.

Downs spoke to reporters on Wednesday around the same time as ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported that he had requested a trade.

Downs was asked directly if he had made that request.

“I’m open to whatever,” Downs said, via James Boyd of TheAthletic.com. “Whatever comes my way, comes my way, and we’ll go from there.”

Downs noted that even with his name in trade rumors, he’s trying to stay in the moment.

“I mean, you think about your future anyway,” Downs said. “So, that’s not really something that’s different. But I feel like it is what it is at the end of the day.

“My feet are here right now, so I’ve got to be right here,” Downs added. “I’ve got a task at hand with my team. So, it could be different tomorrow, could be different the next day — I don’t know. But, just got to be focused on right now.”

That right now includes trying to beat the Jaguars in Jacksonville — a feat the Colts haven’t accomplished since 2014.

“I’m in the game plan, so I’ve got to be ready to go,” Downs said.

But will he still be by the time Sunday rolls around?

That remains to be seen. But based on Tuesday’s trades, the Colts are certainly open for business, particularly as Downs is on an expiring rookie contract.

In seven games this season, Downs has caught 26 passes for 307 yards. Last season, he had 58 receptions for 566 yards with four TDs.

item.title: Shane Steichen: Jonathan Taylor's on our football team, hasn't asked for a trade
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Colts running back Jonathan Taylor's future in Indianapolis is the subject of much scrutiny right now, but head coach Shane Steichen said on Wednesday that Taylor isn't looking for an immediate exit.
item.content:encoded:
Colts running back Jonathan Taylor's future in Indianapolis is the subject of much scrutiny right now, but head coach Shane Steichen said on Wednesday that Taylor isn't looking for an immediate exit.

Steichen told reporters at a Wednesday press conference that Taylor has not asked for a trade in the wake of the team's decision to trade defensive tackle DeForest Buckner and guard Quenton Nelson. Wide receiver Josh Downs reportedly requested a trade on Wednesday and Taylor would likely net the team a rich return to use as part of a rebuilding effort that kicked off with last week's firing of General Manager Chris Ballard.

Steichen acknowledged all of that chatter, but said that he is moving forward with Taylor until told otherwise.

"Those are hypothetical things right now," Steichen said, via Stephen Holder of ESPN.com. "I know there's stuff floating around out there, but JT's on our football team."

Steichen said that it is going to be tough to keep moving forward through the upheaval, but that's "what we signed up for" and the next two weeks will determine just how sweeping the in-season changes are in Indianapolis.

item.title: Budda Baker hasn't asked to be traded, and hasn't asked not to be traded
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Cardinals safety Budda Baker says he's not seeking a trade.
item.content:encoded:
Cardinals safety Budda Baker says he's not seeking a trade. Nor has he expressly asked to stay in Arizona.

Baker, who has often been mentioned as a potential trade target multiple times over the years, told Josh Weinfuss of ESPN on Wednesday that he has not requested a trade, nor has he requested not to be traded. Baker said he hasn't talked to General Manager Monti Ossenfort "about anything."

"My approach is I'm here," Baker said. "I'm here. I want to win. I want to be here. And I'm just controlling what I can control, just taking it one week at a time, and hopefully when the deadline ends, I'll still be here. If not, I mean, it's a business. I understand at the end of the day and that's it."

Baker knows there will be people talking about him as the November 10 trade deadline approaches.

"It's a deadline for a reason," Baker said. "Teams are trying to get players, and our team might be trying to get players and getting other players. So, at the end of the day, it's a business."

Baker is 30 years old and is under contract through 2027 at a salary of about $16 million a season. We'll find out in the next 12 days whether two teams think a Baker trade is good business.

item.title: Cam Heyward: Jared Verse calling Steelers "dirty" will be addressed Sunday
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Dislike between the Browns and Steelers has been brewing for decades, so there isn't much need for any one player to fan the flames of the bad feelings between the two AFC North teams.
item.content:encoded:
Dislike between the Browns and Steelers has been brewing for decades, so there isn't much need for any one player to fan the flames of the bad feelings between the two AFC North teams.

Browns defensive end Jared Verse did that after the two teams played in Week 4, however. Verse explained that he doesn't "have any respect for anybody that plays too dirty and does too much extra s—t after the game" and mentioned double-teaming and sliding while calling his opponents "garbage."

The two teams meet again in Pittsburgh this Sunday and Steelers defensive end Cam Heyward made it clear that Verse's comments haven't been forgotten during an appearance on The Rich Eisen Show this week.

"Double teaming, sliding, chipping, are those not allowed in our game? Yeah, I got the bruises to prove it. But we don't whine about it, baby. It's part of the game," Heyward said Tuesday. "So, I'm looking forward to this game. It's gonna be a fun game. Both teams are in position to do a lot of work in this division, as they say. The AFC North is on fire, and I'm glad I'm in the kitchen because I like it that way. But those were words that were said, and they will be addressed."

The distaste between the two teams is nothing new, but having both of them playing well at the same time is fairly uncommon. With both teams at 5-2 coming into this week, there will be more than bragging rights at stake for the winner.

item.title: Ashton Jeanty: Jets' defense has a couple guys who don't want to tackle
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty is having a terrible year, but he thinks he can turn that around on Sunday against the Jets.
item.content:encoded:
Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty is having a terrible year, but he thinks he can turn that around on Sunday against the Jets.

Jeanty said in the Raiders' locker room on Wednesday that he thinks there are players on the Jets' defense who don't want to tackle him, and that excites him when he sees it on tape.

"I think we can definitely get the run game going," Jeanty said when asked about the Jets' defense. "Get back on track and really get after these guys. A couple guys out there that don't really want to tackle, but I'm not going to say names."

The Raiders started the season 3-0 but are now 3-4. Jeanty said that during this losing streak, he and his teammates are doing a good job of challenging each other to improve without playing the blame game.

"I think the main thing is we've just to to stick together. You lose games, everybody starts questioning things," Jeanty said. "Most importantly, not pointing fingers. Everybody has to work together. It's a team sport."

Jeanty is averaging just 3.1 yards per carry this season, and that needs to improve in a hurry. He believes it can improve, against a Jets defense that allowed Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon to rush for 103 yards and a touchdown last week. If it doesn't improve against a Jets defense that doesn't want to tackle, it may be time to ask bigger questions about why Jeanty can't get going.

item.title: Justin Herbert: Blame for Chargers' offense is on the players, not Mike McDaniel's fault
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Chargers' starting quarterback says the new offensive coordinator does not deserve the blame.
item.content:encoded:
Before the season, Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh predicted that Justin Herbert would be the greatest quarterback ever. During the season, Herbert has been by some measures the worst quarterback in the NFL. That has led to plenty of talk that new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is to blame.

But Herbert says that isn't the case.

"It's not his fault, it's our fault as an offense," Herbert said when asked about McDaniel. "We have to do our job. It's not Mike's fault. The guys are open, plays are being made. It's on us to run, to block, to catch, to throw. It's on us as an offense."

Herbert said that he's learning a lot from McDaniel, even if the results aren't showing up on the field.

"Mike has been very helpful. He's such a great coach and such a great leader, to have the experience and expertise has, it's been very helpful," Herbert said.

According to Herbert, the Chargers' winless season is 100 percent on the players and not at all on McDaniel.

"Mike has done an incredible job of getting people open and it's on us to execute and make plays," Herbert said. "As an offense we have to come together, execute our stuff, and understand that it's on us to fix it."

item.title: Sean McVay doesn't rule out having two kickers on 48-man game-day roster
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: When you have two quarterbacks, you have none.
item.content:encoded:
When you have two quarterbacks, you have none. When you have two kickers, you have a problem.

The Rams, who pivoted to Brandon McManus after losing Blake Grupe (who replaced Harrison Mevis) to a torn ACL, have brought back Joshua Karty to the practice squad. On Wednesday, coach Sean McVay was asked whether he would possibly have two kickers on the 48-man, game-day roster.

“We'll work through all different things," McVay said. "It all depends. When you have 48 bodies and the different guys that are filling in, you have to really ask yourself, 'Okay, does that really make sense? Does it fit?' There are a lot of layers to it so I wouldn't be ready to answer that question yet.”

Karty, a sixth-round pick in 2024, lost the job to Mevis during the 2025 season. He had been out of the NFL after being released by the Cardinals on June 4.

The kicker issue is one of various issues the Rams have with their special teams. In a league where so many games turn on so few moments, a single special-teams glitch can turn a win into a loss.

At 3-4, the Rams can't afford to lose many more games. On Sunday, they get a golden opportunity to get to .500 against the 0-6 Chargers.

item.title: New study estimates 75 percent of former NFL players who died from 2008 to 2023 had CTE
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: A new study from JAMA Network Open by researchers at Boston University, Mass General Brigham, and the Concussion & CTE Foundation has found that an estimated 75 percent of former NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 had CTE.
item.content:encoded:
A new study from JAMA Network Open by researchers at Boston University, Mass General Brigham, and the Concussion & CTE Foundation has found that an estimated 75 percent of former NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 had CTE.

"Many cases may have been early stage at the time of death and possibly symptom free," the paper said, via Shwetha Surendran of ESPN.

That observation speaks to one of the basic realities of CTE. It's unknown how many people have it. And it's no surprise that the vast majority of former NFL players who die with CTE symptoms are later determined to have had CTE.

There's a balance to strike. On one hand, it's obvious that long-term, repetitive head trauma isn't good for the brain. On the other hand, it can be problematic to have hundreds, if not thousands, of former NFL players believing they already have — and constantly fearing the inevitable development of symptoms.

Even now, years after CTE became a commonly-known term, there's much work to be done in order to understand who gets it, how it develops, and what it means to have it. Hopefully, the research will continue with the goal of better clarifying the risks that current players are assuming without making those whose careers have ended unduly anxious about the possibility that a ticking time bomb has been embedded in their brains.

item.title: Sean McVay: Davante Adams "closer to the shorter term" of the 6-10 week timeline
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Rams wide receiver Davante Adams injured his hamstring in an Oct. 18 game against the Cardinals.
item.content:encoded:
Rams wide receiver Davante Adams injured his hamstring in an Oct. 18 game against the Cardinals.

He recently underwent a procedure on the ruptured hamstring.

"Everything's good. It went really well," Rams coach Sean McVay said Wednesday. "He's feeling good in the process of recovering and doing really well.”

The prognosis for Adams was 6-10 weeks, but McVay said that Adams will return probably "closer to the shorter term" of the timeline. That could mean Adams returns sometime after the team's Week 11 off week.

“He tells me, which I believe, [that] he's Wolverine," McVay said. "He'll heal quick and be ready to go. He's in good spirits. [He] sent me a picture the other day [of him] being able to walk already. He’s doing really well, and I think based on how everything went, on the shorter end is what is projected.”

Adams, who is on injured reserve, has 30 receptions for 480 yards and four touchdowns in six games.

item.title: For PFT's 25th anniversary, completely re-written Quarterback of the Future is coming
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The 25th anniversary of the launch of PFT happens on Sunday, November 1.
item.content:encoded:
The 25th anniversary of the launch of PFT happens on Sunday, November 1. And for those of you who have been here since the early days of the site's existence, I've made you something.

I've completely re-written Quarterback of the Future, the long-forgotten football/sci-fi novel that helped lead me into this business in the first place.

I won't bore you with the details of how it all happened here. (I'll bore you with the details of how it all happened here, in the official introduction to the book I'll post one chapter at a time free of charge.)

Also, here's the landing page for the various chapters. The plan is to post one per day. (They're relatively short.) Depending on the response, my mood at any given moment, and whether time permits, I may accelerate the process.

Regardless, it's a brand-new version of a solid story that was, frankly, not very well written. After years of writing thousands of words per day (and writing eight or nine novels — I've lost track — along with Playmakers), the second try is better.

As I'm reminded whenever I flip through a copy of the original QBF, it can't be much worse.

Take it for whatever it is. It should be fun. It should be enjoyable. Each chapter should make you interested in reading the next one.

Give it a try. Chapter One arrives Sunday, the official 25th anniversary of the moment we first went live.

item.title: Troy Aikman says there's a "50-50 chance" he won't be working in TV next year
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Hall of Fame quarterback Troy Aikman appeared at a Dallas event on Wednesday night with Peter King, in connection with Peter's new book, The Game.
item.content:encoded:
Hall of Fame quarterback Troy Aikman appeared at a Dallas event on Wednesday night with Peter King, in connection with Peter's new book, The Game. During the session, Aikman addressed whether he'd be calling NFL games in 2027. Along the way, Aikman addressed the Babar in the bookstore.

Via veteran sports journalist Tim Cowlishaw, Aikman said there's a "50-50 chance" that Aikman won't be working in TV next year.

Given the circumstances, that seems accurate. Aikman's contract expires after the Super Bowl, and he has not been bashful when it comes to expressing concern (and exasperation) with ESPN's lack of interest in negotiating an extension.

If he leaves ESPN, where else will he go? With CBS already deciding to make J.J. Watt the replacement for Tony Romo, a prime seat will be available for Aikman only if Prime Video opts to exercise its ability to buy out Kirk Herbstreit and pivot to Aikman.

It's no surprise, then, that Aikman has been talking about possibly working for the Cowboys. He has spoken about wanting to work in a front office, and his consulting gig with the Dolphins may have been the first step toward a Matt Millen/John Lynch-style pivot.
